Bill.BriefDescription: Regarding information sharing in child dependency cases.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to information sharing in child dependency cases;amending RCW 13.34.350; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that to aid in theprevention of tragic deaths of children in the child welfare system,those responsible for making placement decisions in cases of childabuse or neglect should have the relevant evidence available to them toaid them in making placement decisions that will best protect thesafety and welfare of the child.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 13.34.350 and 2001 c 52 s 2 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) In order to facilitate communication of information needed toserve the best interest of any child who is the subject of a dependencycase filed under this chapter, the department of social and healthservices shall, consistent with state and federal law governing therelease of confidential information, establish guidelines, and shalluse those guidelines for the facilitation of communication of relevant p. 1 SB 5666information among divisions, providers, the courts, the family,caregivers, caseworkers, and others. (2) Notwithstanding subsection (1) of this section, in any casewith findings of child abuse or neglect, the following information ordocuments must be made available to the persons listed in subsection(3) of this section, when applicable, before the implementation of anyplacement decision of a child, including inhome placement: (a) Health care information regarding the child, including but notlimited to physician or other medical professional records, reports,notes, or letters regarding the child; (b) Substance abuse treatment records if treatment is ordered bythe court or a placement agreement, including a voluntary placementagreement; (c) Mental health treatment records if treatment is ordered by thecourt or a placement agreement, including a voluntary placementagreement; (d) Other information or documents as required by the department. (3) The information or documents listed in subsection (2) of thissection must be made available, in their entirety, to the followingpersons, when applicable, before the implementation of any placementdecision of a child, including inhome placement: (a) Any caseworker assigned to the case; (b) Any supervisor of a caseworker assigned to the case; (c) Any court hearing a matter relating to the dependency of thechild; (d) Any member of a child protection team assigned to the case; (e) Any guardian ad litem assigned to the case; (f) A parent, guardian, or custodian of the child; and (g) A parent's, guardian's, or custodian's counsel. (4) A copy of the original information or document listed insubsection (2) of this section must be provided to every party referredto in subsection (3) of this section. (5) Any sharing of information or documents under this sectionshall be consistent with state and federal law governing the release ofconfidential information.
